articleTitle: TLM enhancements for EMC studies
abstract: The enhancement of the 3-D transmission-line matrix method (TLM) to include electromagnetic field penetration into thin lossy films, interaction with fine wires and coupling through narrow slot apertures is described. The models are tested against theoretical results and fine discretisation TLM models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Shielding theory and practice
abstract: A cursory look is taken at the constraints and conditions consistent with Maxwell's laws and equations and Maxwell's laws using Schelkunoff's recommended approximation (i.e. using the analogy between conducted waves and radiated waves). The value of the shielding quality of metallic materials developed using Kirchhoff's laws and circuit theory are fully documented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMI and EMC in high voltage energy systems
abstract: This paper reports on part of a research project titled 'Condition Monitoring of High Voltage Equipment'. EMC activities include study and measurement of electromagnetic fields and transient in high voltage/high power installations such as power substations. The project involves applying and developing advanced modelling and measuring techniques for electromagnetic interferences and establishing criteria for assessment of equipment for electromagnetic compatibilities. The paper covers calculations already performed as well as those planned in the near future.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Propagation and suppression of interfering transients on multiconductor transmission line systems
abstract: Extended transmission line systems are of special interest concerning overvoltage protection for sensitive line terminations. The time dependent behaviour of the line currents, induced by interfering electromagnetic fields, essentially depends on the line length and the line terminations. Primary interfering currents will be generated on the line shield and, dependent on the transfer impedance of the shield, these currents will penetrate the shield and induce currents on the inner conductors. The simulation of interfering currents on a widely extended transmission line system will be discussed. Additionally the transient response of protection circuits against interfering transients for the protection of sensitive amplifier inputs is within this transmission line system is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Open site PCS telepoint intrasystem interference analysis and computation
abstract: Open site operations of Telepoint micro or nano cells are vulnerable to intrasystem mutual interference effects, especially due to line-of-sight propagation conditions common to several cosited user sets. Analysis of mutual interference effects and computation results contribute to develop useful criteria for Telepoint system reliable operation under realistic worst-case cosited conditions. The application of efficient interference mitigation methods is also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An optical instrumentation using one sensor with an ANC hybrid IC
abstract: The authors previously developed an Alternating Noise Cancelling (ANC) method using a sensor-dummy and a dual sensor on an optical instrumentation that could cancel noise on the transmission line. A revised method using a hybrid IC is presented and its accuracy verified by experiments using sinusoidal waves and others.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International standardization of immunity to high altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP)
abstract: The International Electrotechnical Commission has initiated such standardization and eleven nations are permanent members of the Sub-Committee TC 77C which has been formed within the IEC Technical Committee on Electromagnetic Compatibility. A five-part proposed outline of work is presented and some new proposals are listed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing for the shielding quality of EMI gaskets and gasketed joints
abstract: This paper deals with the generation, propagation and suppression of radiated EM waves through metallic shielding barriers and gasketed joints. It describes (1) the correlation between the transfer impedance of a gasketed joint and the subsequent shielding effectiveness of the joint; (2) a transfer impedance test fixture; and (3) the transfer impedance test data of selected gaskets and joint surfaces.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband absorbers and applications in absorptive ground-mats (AOATS's) and wall coverings of absorber lined chambers (ALC's)
abstract: This paper looks deeper into the concepts of such absorbers, considering first of all their basic performance: the wave 'Reflection' for normal incidence for the 30 MHz-1 GHz frequency range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the time domain three dimensional finite difference method to a wide variety of EMC problems
abstract: The problems include lightning, nuclear EMP, and magnetic field shielding effectiveness. Subject matter include aircraft, partially buried faculties and communication shelters. Emphasis is placed on comparison of numerical results with experimental results in order to validate the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Certification and accreditation in the EC
abstract: The paper describes briefly the directives concerning the conformity assessment procedures the CE mark, the specific provisions related to EMC and telecommunication terminal equipment and the testing bodies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMView-3-dimensional representation of antenna patterns for visualization of EM radiation envelopes
abstract: This paper presents a new and advanced method for generating a 3-dimensional colour representation of radiation patterns of a broadcast facility. This presentation visualizes the radiation pattern of the antennae, in 2-D and 3-D color representation for radiation hazard and electromagnetic interference evaluation. Utilizing this system, the designers, users and operators of the facility can evaluate the capability of the station to meet its operational goals, as well as the hazard zones both on ground and in the air, in the vicinity of the facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLF method: elimination of noises and quantitative interpretation
abstract: Geophysical investigations by the very low frequency method are greatly complicated by time variations and the rugged-relief effect. For elimination of these noises effective statistical procedures have been developed. Quantitative interpretation of VLF anomalies under difficult geological conditions can be conducted with modified methods, developed in magnetic prospecting. Over complex geological sections interpretation of the method's integration can be conducted using original logical-informational algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of special EMI absorption filters for high-power microwave transmitters
abstract: This paper describes the design of special filters which reduce the undesired broadband spurious spectrum by 40 to 80 dB in a large frequency band, up to the fourth harmonic of the MW transmitter carrier frequency. The insertion losses in the transmitter passband are less than 0.3 dB. The physical dimensions and weight of the proposal filters are significantly less than for conventional transmitters. The performances of the designed filters are discussed and suggestions for future improvements presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of bulk current injection in susceptibility testing of automotive electronics
abstract: Theory and special aspects of BCI in combination with the electromagnetic compatibility of automotive electronics are treated. The influence of geometrical and electrical parameters in a typical test arrangement is investigated. The usefulness of this test method in the laboratory and on board test vehicles is demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computation and measurements of electromagnetic fields generated by a medium wave antenna array: how close to it would you reside?
abstract: Concern was raised regarding the electromagnetic radiation levels from a high power medium wave broadcast station in Israel. The authors conducted an analysis, based on the Method of Moments in order to assess the electric and magnetic field strengths expected on the boundaries of the facility, as well as in the intended village. Good agreement was found between computed and measured levels. It was found that both the electric and magnetic field strength levels were below the Radiation Safety Guidelines established by the WHO/IRPA/INIRC, thus allowing some growth potential for the radio facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMI gaskets and their correct application
abstract: The paper begins with some brief theory as to how a gasket maintains the electrical continuity of a shield, and then describes in detail the best methods. Emphasis is placed on surface finish and a computer aided groove design programme, as well as the importance of performing physical and electrical tests on gaskets to provide long term quality assurance. A number of new innovative gasket materials and their benefits are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Einstein's approach to understanding electromagnetic fields as part of matter in EMC
abstract: Einstein's approach to matter as part of electromagnetic field is elaborated with an understanding of basic state of matter being the continuous state. The origin of induced electric field vortex is surface divergence of magnetic field, Div (cB). This fact can be measured with many electrical devices and is obviously logical when electric and magnetic fields are understood as part of matter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The solution for fast and reproducible emission and susceptibility measurements: GTEM cells
abstract: The use of a TEM-cell anechoic-chamber hybrid, the GTEM cell for EMI testing is discussed. The hybrid chamber may be used for both susceptibility testing (the TEM mode simulates a plane wave) and radiated emission measurements (data are correlated to ground screen results via a multi-pole model). This paper stresses reproducibility in emission measurements, namely, that emission results do not depend on either the test object location within the cell or its starting orientation. Experimental data for a self contained spherical dipole and a laptop computer demonstrate this point.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accumulative effects of two modulated RF signals on the EMI susceptibility of the mu A741 operational amplifier
abstract: Measurements of the demodulating characteristics for one and two modulated RF inputs are presented. The implications of these results on the evaluation of electronic equipment susceptibility are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modelling of indirect lightning return stroke effects
abstract: The paper presents a modelling procedure for evaluating the voltages and currents induced on transmission lines by nearby lightning. Models are needed in order to evaluate lightning effects where experimental results are not available. These models allow better design and coordination of the protection of power and telecommunication networks against lightning induced effects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Highly linear low noise amplifiers for interference-immune receiving system
abstract: A set of broadband low noise interference-immune amplifier modules comprising matched broadband amplifiers and matched filters is described. In the frequency band 1-100 MHz these devices ensure a low noise figure, high dynamic range, matching in a wide frequency band, stability, identity of parameters, versatility, and high compatibility of stationary and mobile systems. Connection of modules makes it possible to implement a complicated amplifier system with the specified amplitude-frequency response and low level of amplitude and phase errors. The parameters and characteristics of modules, their design features and principles are given. The amplification system of the largest UTR-2 decameter band radiotelescope is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC testing with millisecond surge pulses
abstract: Transient overvoltages or surges generated by the most varied of causes, frequently occur in mains voltage networks. Particularly energy-rich are the surges that result when a fuse blows. Such transients have pulse widths extending into the region of milliseconds. These transients containing very high energy could damage electronic equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radiated emissions test-performance of the GHz TEM cell: a comparison with open area test site (OATS) compliance measurements
abstract: This article describes the direct comparison of results of four series of tests. Two differing comparisons are described; a full personal computer system tested per the requirements of ANSI 63.4. Draft 11.4, and two separate sets of dipole measurements. Good agreement of results has been found.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The correlation of the geomagnetic field and radon density, and its relation to biological effects
abstract: Data of geomagnetic and radon variations have been analyzed on the basis of underground measurements under nearly constant temperature and humidity. The correlation was established and it was shown that in order to evaluate discrete concentrations of radon and its biological applications, it is necessary to take into account its temporary function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time-domain analysis of multiconductor cables
abstract: This paper predicts crosstalk and coupling between cables and electromagnetic fields. In the quasi-TEM assumption and frequency-domain, the response of a system containing an arbitrary number of multiconductor transmission lines (MTL) with arbitrary linear networks in an electromagnetic field is given. Time-domain analytical solutions are given for two and three conductors illuminated by an external field. More generally, several time and frequency domain experimental and numerical results related to shielded and unshielded cables are presented. Some examples of nonuniform lines (cascaded networks) are performed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Close-fit modelling of high ULF magnetic fields preceding Loma Prieta earthquake
abstract: The earthquake of 1989 Oct.17 was preceded for over two weeks by ULF magnetic noise anomalies with a very high peak about three hours before the event. The model in this paper, using parameter values based almost totally on data from local seismology and geological resistivity structure, predicts the anomalies to relatively high accuracies over three orders of magnitude of ULF.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic shielding of circular and rectangular connectors, backshells and braid terminations
abstract: This paper discusses electromagnetic coupling in both circular and rectangular connectors and backshells by presenting measurements of the surface transfer impedance contributions of each of the major design features.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Shielding options for plastic enclosures
abstract: Comparative advatages, disadvantages and costs are presented for Zn arc spray, vacuum metallisation and electroless plating, filled conductive plastics and resin bonded conductive coatings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Immunity testing of large systems
abstract: This paper suggests some tests already carried out for single apparatus or small systems, but adapted to larger applications and corresponding to well-known electromagnetic phenomena.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Is EMC modelling useful for standardization?
abstract: The developments in EMC modelling permit to estimate the disturbances in different kinds of circuits and installations, to define a protection philosophy and to evaluate its efficiency. Using some examples of modelling, the paper discusses whether these possibilities are useful for the standardization in progress in the European Community. It is shown that essential progress has been made in the last years in modelling field-to-transmission line coupling, crosstalk, antennas, and shielded enclosures and that these models can be applied to define parameters and environments needed for standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing the immunity of electronic equipment to RF fields-current injection testing vs. radiated testing
abstract: The contribution deals with the different aspects of testing for instance with sources of electromagnetic fields and their amplitude dependence, external and internal resonances, conversion of electromagnetic fields into currents and voltages on cables and surfaces, characteristic impedances of antennas and transmission lines, coupling of test signals onto cables, decoupling of auxiliary devices, necessary to operate the EUT, and the influence of the cable arrangement within radiation tests. Both methods are defined within the international standards IEC 801-3 (radiated) and IEC 801-6 (conducted). The paper concludes with a status report of these standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New aspects in the EMC standardization basic, generic and product standards
abstract: An overview of work related to electrical and electronic equipment in the international and European standardization organizations IEC and CENELEC gives information on coming developments. The relevant organizations, the disturbance phenomena, the various types and subjects of EMC standards, the status of these (end of 1992), the different types of products and the legal and contractual status of EMC standards are covered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical approaches to immunity standardization for telecommunication equipment in Japan
abstract: A method is proposed for calibrating field strength in anechoic chambers for points less than 0.8 m high. A method using a two-wire rhombic antenna is proposed for immunity testing at frequencies less than 30 MHZ. A method using a GTEM cell for testing small equipment provides the economy of standard TEM cell testing without having to use an anechoic chamber. An advanced conductive immunity test circuit is proposed which allows voltages of up to 100 V to be applied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CATV leakage control using a GPS based system
abstract: The introduction of the Cumulative Leakage Index method by the FCC has constituted a step in the right direction. This method recognizes that there is no CATV system without leakages, and tries to limit the number of permissible leakages according to their intensity. The criterion is a calculated dimensionless number based on the cumulative effect of all leakages of the system at a height of 3000 m above the centre. A computer-controlled system including a field strength meter and a GPS receiver is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coupling of multiwire shielded cables to a lightning discharge
abstract: This paper describes a theoretical and experimental approach of the coupling of the electromagnetic field radiated by a lightning discharge to overhead telecommunication cables. These behave as multiwire shielded lines and the intrinsic shielding parameters such as the transfer impedances are first deduced from measurements. Then, by calculation of the field illuminating the cable, the disturbing voltages are determined and compared with values obtained on an experimental site.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Open Field Test Site attenuation repeatability in accordance with FCC/OET 55
abstract: As of 1 June 1991 Federal Communication Commission lists 190 Contract Test Sites: 103 of these are located in the USA, 39 in Japan, 11 in Taiwan, seven in Canada, five in Germany, four in England and only one in Israel. Hermon Labs. Open Field Test Site was built in the beginning of 1988 and listed with FCC from June 1988. In spite of FCC demands every three years for recalibrations (site attenuation measurements) Hermon Labs. is doing this measurement each half year. An analysis of the measurements is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An interference analysis on cellular mobile radiocommunications using CAD/CAE techniques
abstract: The cochannel interference in a base-station's receiver of one cell produced by a mobile in another cell that uses the same frequency is studied. An OMNISYS simulation model of channel-plus-receiver is proposed and used to carry out an interference analysis. Conclusions over the cell size and the cluster size of a cellular mobile radio system are obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Composite and exoatmospheric EMP influence on naval vessels
abstract: Protection from EMP can be afforded by utilizing the natural screening inherent in the ship's metallic construction, and by hardening vulnerable equipment. This paper discusses the general characteristics of NEMP, LEMP and HPM and the measures necessary to ensure that the vessel's operational capabilities are not seriously impaired.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trends in electromagnetic compatibility for radio communication and radar systems: analysis computation and mitigation methods
abstract: If efficient and drastic EMC regulation policy will not be applied, radio services and systems will mutually disturb themselves and deteriorate, and chaos may result. Noise and EMI mitigation must be applied from the start of system design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The obstacles of magnetotelluric sounding connected with inhomogeneities of the initial wave
abstract: Inside special regions on the ground surface magnetotelluric sounding curve interpretation may lead to false results. Such regions occupy a radius within 500 km from the base of the resonance line. To obtain a reliable result it is necessary to find a spatial structure of the pulsation fields. It is enough to have two or three observation points to reconstruct the initial resonance structure. Further procedures of magnetotelluric sounding interpretation must include calculations of the spatial field spectrum and spectral impedance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Composite shielding: modeling and verification
abstract: Models of composites are explained and finite element applications shown. Closed form subroutines are justified in the light of complex permittivity and permeability measurement verification. Shielding effectiveness is derived on the basis of these complex parameters and the proposed appropriate model for the composite materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coherent (amplitude and phase) measurements for EMC
abstract: This paper shows the power of coherent measurement technique in EMI/EMC. It demonstrates the benefit of (1) measuring a filter's scattering parameters to obtain a powerline differential mode and common mode insertion loss and the filter's transfer functions; (2) measuring the shielding effectiveness of materials using a TEM cell and a vector network analyzer; (3) characterization of RF environment in the time domain, and (4) analyzing the effect of an inductive coupling device on coupled signal waveform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wire coupling analysis in large systems
abstract: A software system for analysing wire coupling in large systems such as aircraft is presented. Its purpose is to improve EMC certification effectiveness by indicating potentially hazardous couplings between specific wires, which can be checked specifically during the experimental EMC proof tests. The system requires a relatively simple data collection process, unspecified items being defined by a simple default insertion system. Comparisons with experiment are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of re-radiated emission from power cord
abstract: Radiation emission from a product with an AC power cord can be larger than from a product without an AC power cord between 30 and 200 MHz. This indirect RF current induced from a RF source of another outer antenna is different for AC power cord arrangements and earthing methods. This paper reports sample data and assumed cause of power cord effects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurements of screening effectiveness of cables assemblies over broad frequency range
abstract: The screening effectiveness against currents is expressed in terms of the transfer ZT and against charges (i.e. electric fields and voltages) in terms of the capacitive coupling impedance ZF (or associated parameters). For electrically long cables both effects act at the same time; therefore a separation of ZT and ZF is not necessary from the viewpoint of the user. Either equivalent transfer impedance or the screening attenuation may be an adequate measure (the typical criterion for an electrically long cable may be taken as L/20<or=1 whereby L=300/(f/MHz)).<<ETX>>

articleTitle: A probabilistic approach to the problem of crosstalk between wires
abstract: This paper treats the problem of coupling between a pair of wires (over a ground plane) having a random separation which is bounded within known limits. A probability distribution function provides a trustworthy means of evaluating the extent of the coupling. The methodology presented may provide a basis for generalization to more complex problems such as wires in bundles or winding wires.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ray analysis of electromagnetic scattering for a coupled parallel plate waveguide
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic plane wave scattering by a coupled, perfectly-conducting, semi-infinite two-dimensional parallel plate waveguide, with a thin, uniform layer of lossy material on its inner walls is analyzed using a a high frequency method. When the waveguide is illuminated by a plane wave, the ray fields are coupled into the waveguide from the exterior region and found via the Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD) ray method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution of severe cardiovascular events under changing cosmophysical and meteorologic conditions. Forecasting possibilities
abstract: The goals of this one-year study (1990) were to check the distribution of certain events in accordance with different levels of geomagnetic activity (GMA); and to determine whether combined geomagnetic- meteorologic data provide an improved basis for studying and predicting the forthcoming distribution of such events. The study was carried out at a 1000-bed multiple university hospital. In all, 692 admissions for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), 79 deaths from AMI, and 51 deaths from cerebrovascular accident were studied.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Case history: magnetic interference from a power supply to a computer terminal-magnetic shielding was the solution!
abstract: This paper discusses interference to a video display terminal which was rack-mounted in the near vicinity of a high current switch mode AC power supply. Preliminary testing showed that the interference (visualized as 'waves' on the screen) was due to low frequency magnetic interference emanating from the (non-shielded) power supply. The installation of magnetic shielding over the power supply eliminated the problem. Results are presented of measurements of the magnetic fields at the VDT location both prior to and after the application of magnetic shielding and recommendations for future designs are detailed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field parameters of circular low frequency current near the Earth's surface
abstract: An influence of the surface is determined and practical calculation expressions are given. It is shown that in some near surroundings of the source a secondary field due to the Earth's surface, depends on its magnetic properties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Achieving EMC in a LDRS system (laser designation and rangefinding)
abstract: The paper describes the EMC design of the system with regard to specification, management, mechanical design, filtering, harnessing circuits, PCB and grounding concept. Test results from EMC qualification tests are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application and performance characteristics of resin bonded shielding coatings
abstract: Ag, Ni and Cu coatings are compared and the electrical and mechanical properties and environmental stability are considered from the test aspect.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A medium size NEMP radiation system used in a shielded room
abstract: A bounded wave transmission line ENP simulator which achieves a very good confinement of the field inside its volume is described. Results of field mapping in free space and inside a shielded room are presented. These measurements have shown that the field decays very rapidly outside the structure, making it possible to use the antenna without disturbing its environment. It was also shown that when the simulator is used inside a Faraday cage, the reflections from the walls of the room do not produce significant field distortions within the working volume.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of low frequency electric and magnetic fields in gene expression in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstract: Low energy electric and magnetic fields (<300 Hz) induce changes in gene activities as measured by increases in some transcript levels. The present study confirms these observations and extends them from diptera and mammalian cells to yeast. It shows that the effects are gene specific, that the gene remains 'on' for a relatively short period of time, and that a refractory period is necessary before the gene can be restimulated. There is a correlation between response to such fields and to other cellular stress responses suggesting that the cell 'sees' the signal as a stress. Models to explain the interaction of EM fields with cells are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC standard for ITE and telecommunications
abstract: A number of emission standards are used by various national administrations but the requirements and test methods are generally based on the emission standard developed by CISPR Publication 22. The standard is based upon a technical rationale considering receiver density and immunity the requirements being to allow radio services of all types to operate as intended. An explanation of amendments being considered is addressed, as well as an amendment introduced by ETSI covering the testing of physically large telecommunication systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Regulations of the European Communities regarding electromagnetic compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the scope of the Directive 89/336/EEC of May 1989, its main provisions, the rules of application for the different products, the placing on the market and the putting into service, and the timetable for implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Guiding principles in national RF spectrum management
abstract: The RF Spectrum in Israel is managed by the Ministry of Communication. The basis for frequency allotments to the various services is the Radio Regulations of the ITU. The guiding principles of a defined policy are suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application for FCC verification, notification, certification and type approval
abstract: Extended summary form only given. The authors present some conclusions on almost three years experience of servicing of Israeli Industry (low power transmitters and receivers for hearing aids, control of movements, acknowledgement systems, etc.) according to the new version of Part 15 of the FCC standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital terrain models applied to the C/I ratio determination in frequency reduce design
abstract: A tool is developed to plan cellular systems based on the application of theoretical studies of propagation phenomena in urban areas to the real digital terrain models of a city. This permits the design of the cellular structure in an interactive way taking account of the real interference and ambiguity zones. Methods for the reduction of cochannel interference are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the optimization of frequency assignment in developing networks
abstract: Some assignment strategies are investigated and compared, assuming the presence of not only intersite but also cosite constraints. The influence of intermodulation interference on the capacity of the frequency band is estimated in both 'pure' dynamic and dynamic-static statements. The latter includes a back-tracking phase with partial reassignment of currently assigned requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of the stochastic irregularities on the conductivity of the ionosphere
abstract: The study was carried out for large scale inhomogeneities and quasistationary electromagnetic fields. It is shown that Pedersen conductivity sharply increases in a strong geomagnetic field even for small stochastic irregularities of the electron density. The evaluations show that this peculiarity has to be taken into account during analysis of ionospheric and magnetospheric measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the possibility of the above ionosphere ULF waves electromagnetic sounding of the Earth
abstract: The relations connecting the amplitude and phase of the hydromagnetic waves above the ionosphere with the impedance of the Earth are obtained. It is shown that at large distances from the incident hydromagnetic wave beam axis the apparent resistivity depends mostly on the features of the geoelectrical section, and practically does not depend on the distribution of the field inside the beam. The 'above-ionospheric' curves of apparent resistivity are calculated for middle latitude pulsations excited by the field-line resonance oscillations. It is found that information about geoelectric profile may be obtained from the polarization pattern of the fields at satellite heights and also from simultaneous ground-based and satellite magnetometric observations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis and characteristics of a new class of intrinsically conducting polymers, obtained from functionalization of polyacetylene-like materials
abstract: A new class of intrinsically conducting polymers, starting from dehydrochlorinated PVC, can be provided without instability in air. Consequently, the authors propose a stable polyacetylene-like material, with high electrical conductivity, for electromagnetic interference and radio-frequency interference shielding. The first measurements of the elementary electromagnetic parameters ( in * and mu *) have proved that they are especially effective to shield an electric field, with an attenation higher than 40 dB in the range of 30 MHz-3 GHz. Other applications may be available especially in the field of absorbent materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC compliance measurements in the 1990s: new challenges call for innovative solutions
abstract: Alternative EMC test techniques are considered, as well as their potential for regulatory authority acceptance. The major topics are conducted vs. radiated measurements, free space test environment, GTEM cells, stirred mode chambers, and use of active antennas. The main thrust is on radiated emissions testing, although some aspects of radiated immunity testing are also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interference analyzer protection in conducted emission measurements of high current consumption circuits
abstract: An interference analyzer is a sophisticated, highly sensitive instrument with very low permissible AC (maximum +20 dBm) and DC (0 V) input power. Some spectrum analyzers have separate protected inputs for conducted emission measurements. Such protection does not work when high power very narrow ( mu sec/nsec) spikes occur. Hermon Laboratories developed a low-cost, very effective device with six levels of protection. The device has total 0 dB gain attenuation with +or-0.5 dB flatness over the 10 kHz-30 MHz frequency range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MIL-E-6051D safety margin requirements for electro-explosive devices EED-a new measurement method
abstract: A susceptibility test of devices exposed to the electromagnetic environment of the system requires 20 dB safety margins. In order to verify these there are several test methods based on measuring the RF current. flowing through the EED. The involvement of the measuring sensor in the EED's circuit causes problems of electromagnetic energy penetration through the sensor's wires and thus the accuracy of the current measurement is degraded. The suggested test method eliminates this problem by replacing the EED with a fuse. If the fuse is not blown during the test, it is understood that the maximum current is less then indicated by the fuse data sheet, and this current is used in evaluation of the safety margins.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Protection of buried telecommunication cables against high amplitude transient currents
abstract: This paper evaluates the protective effects due to a bare conductor embedded near a buried telecommunication cable when high amplitude currents flow in the ground. This phenomenon usually occurs when high power lines, running parallel to telecommunication cables, are struck by a lightning discharge producing an arc between a phase conductor and the ground. Many numerical examples show the effects of the various parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A systematic method for the risk analysis of an electronic system under field EMI conditions
abstract: A systematic and quantitative method is presented for the evaluation of EMC performance in immunity tests. It is possible to optimise the EMC costs and quality of an electronic system. The verification of this method will be completed by experiments and simulations during the next two years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated radiated electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) test system
abstract: The development of an Automated Susceptibility Test Set is discussed with reference to electrical and system characteristics and field levelling in three modes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Equipment lightning protection methods
abstract: Telecommunication protectors differ from power protectors in that there is not power follow-on current to be interrupted, and operating voltages are of a much lower order. Due to the large number of protected circuits, the protector must be small and cheap, and it must be capable of sustaining many more discharges than a protector on a power route.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Four ways to analyse geomagnetic activity and medical related events
abstract: Four methods of comparing geomagnetic activity (GMA) and medical-biological events are discussed: (1) daily A and K indices, (2) 'peristorm' days analysis, (3) mean monthly K index, and (4) daily number of events on quiet (I degrees ), unsettled (II degrees ), active (III degrees ) and stormy (IV degrees ) GMA days in the complete rising and declining parts of the 11-year solar activity cycle.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC for low-frequency conducted disturbances-international standards and their technical background
abstract: The paper presents the technical and economic aspects of electromagnetic compatibility especially for 'harmonics', 'unbalance', 'voltage fluctuations, dips and interruptions'. Causes and effects of these disturbances are tackled as well as their superposition and propagation on the different voltage levels of electric supply systems. Derived from these deliberations the existing and currently prepared International Standards and Guides on the limitation of the emission and the immunity as well as on the definition of the necessary measurement and test methods are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solution of EMC problems via analysis methods: a review
abstract: A comprehensive review is conducted of the most common and presently used analytical tools in the analysis and prediction of EMI. The study outlines the early fundamentals behind the theory of LRC network representation in the coupling mechanisms between noise-source and susceptible circuit elements. The work is extended to include the latest in computational electromagnetic techniques for the analysis of complex topological EMC problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 1992 Regional Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility "1992 - From a Unified Region to a Unified World" (Cat. No.92TH0463-0)
abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.
